reader.requirement: At --std 85 the clauses of a relative file's FD (BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD in each of its three formats, LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF, DATA RECORDS, and the IPC module's GLOBAL/EXTERNAL) must be accepted in any order, each bound with the same effect wherever it is written.

edition-consulted.switches: row.At(DialectLevel) picks the edition's figure; the FD row has Sequence null (order free) and no EarlierFigure, so 85 and 2023 read the same row
LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF and DATA RECORDS accepted at 85 and refused from 2002 (VisitValueOfClause, VisitDataRecordsClause likewise); position-independent

reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf22_02 writes DATA/LABEL/RECORD CONTAINS/BLOCK reversed; VALUE OF, RECORD VARYING DEPENDING ON, BLOCK integer TO integer and GLOBAL out of printed order are not exercised

probes.printed: R2=CDEFGH LEN=0006 ST=00 / R1=AB LEN=0002 ST=00
probes.expected: VALUE OF, DATA RECORDS, RECORD VARYING FROM 2 TO 6 DEPENDING ON, LABEL, BLOCK 2 TO 4 in reversed order accepted; the variable-length records round-trip with their lengths

probes.printed: COBOL6849 DATA RECORDS NOT-A-REC (clause written first) and COBOL2604 LINAGE not a clause of a relative FD
probes.expected: a clause written first is still bound and screened by its own rules; a clause outside the relative FD format is refused wherever it stands

probes.printed: only COBOL0900 for the 2002 AS phrase; RECORD, IS GLOBAL, LABEL, IS EXTERNAL out of order accepted
probes.expected: order free at 85; the later edition's AS phrase refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.3.2.3 SR2  (3.2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: The grammar takes fileDescriptionClause+ with no order, the binder dispatches each clause by kind, and the clause-order screen's FD row is order-free at every edition. Side observation outside this rule: RECORD CONTAINS 9 TO 3 CHARACTERS on a relative FD compiled clean at 85 (fdord3.cob); the 1985 Format 3 RECORD clause prints no syntax rule on that order, so it is not judged here.

refuter.evidence: fd1.cob (--std 85), orders the reader did not run clean (fdord4 compiled only beside a COBOL0900): FD REL-F BLOCK 3 / IS GLOBAL / VALUE OF FILE-ID IS WS-NAME (data-name operand) / LABEL RECORD STANDARD / RECORD CONTAINS 2 TO 6 (Format 2, CHARACTERS omitted) / DATA RECORD REC-S REC-L; FD REL-X LABEL RECORDS OMITTED / RECORD 4 / IS EXTERNAL (EXTERNAL last). Compiled and ran: 'W 00 00', and the contained program FD1IN read the GLOBAL file written out of order: 'R1 AB ... 00', 'R2 CDEFGH 00'. The first run was refused only by §1985:VIII.4.9.3 SR3 (WRITE without INVALID KEY, COBOL6826), which shows the 1985 relative arm is the one taken.
